To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a spontaneous trend exists between the incidence of PVCs and the length of cardiac cycle and that this relationship seems to remain stable in the same patient over time.

the relationship between the incidence of PVCs and the length of preceding cardiac cycles is reproducible in most patients with frequent PVCs and can be identified by simple linear regression analysis.
the percentage of premature ventricular complexes (PVCs)/hour was related to the preceding RR interval in patients with frequent PVCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between the incidence of premature ventricular complexes and the preceding heart rate in patients with frequent premature complexes.
the identification of a spontaneous trend between ventricular arrhythmia and the length of a preceding cardiac cycle.

the study of the relationship between the occurrence of ventricular arrhythmic events (premature ventricular contractions) and the preceding heart rate, in order to identify the dynamic behavior of the ventricular arrhythmia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamic behavior of the PVCs is reproducible in a large proportion of patients.
a tachycardiadependent behavior of ventricular premature beats can be identified in a large percentage of patients with ventricular arrhythmia.
the incidence of ventricualr arrhythmias is related to the preceding cardiac cycle and this relationship remains stable over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a relationship between the heart rate and the occurrence of PVCs.
the relationship between PVC and heart rate is not random and can be reproducibly assessed by 24-hr monitoring.
the incidence of ventricualr arrhythmias is dependent on heart rate and the direction of the dependence can be identified by a simple statistical analysis of 24 hour Holter recordings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to characterize the dynamic behavior of PVCs in patients with frequent premature contractions.
the dynamic behavior of PVCs at different heart rates can be used as a tool for risk stratification.
the dynamic behavior of PVCs at different heart rates is a stable characteristic of the arrhythmia.
